The ego agent prioritizes ball possession over defending its own goal.
The ego agent positions itself to receive passes from the teammate when in proximity.
The ego agent stays primarily between the ball and its own goal when defending.
The ego agent attempts to intercept opponent passes by predicting their path.
The ego agent avoids long, risky dribbles that could lead to loss of possession.
The ego agent maintains appropriate spacing to avoid crowding the teammate.
The ego agent advances toward the opponent's goal when the ball is in the opponent's half.
The ego agent relies on implicit environmental cues rather than explicit signaling to coordinate with the teammate.
